futureYou.personTheyWillBecome: You will become a confident, dual-skilled technology professional in Da Nang's growing tech scene — a QA engineer who can catch bugs with automated test suites in Playwright or Cypress, and a frontend contributor who ships React-powered UI components that teams actually rely on. Employers like AvePoint, SmartOSC, and DX Tech will not just call you back — they will compete for you, because you will carry something rare: deep QA discipline fused with real frontend development ability. You will be the engineer who bridges quality and delivery, earns the trust of senior developers and product managers alike, and owns features from first line of code to final sign-off.
futureYou.achievementSummary: By the end of this roadmap you will have landed your first full-time QA or junior frontend role in Da Nang, built and deployed at least three portfolio projects with live URLs and public GitHub repositories, achieved proficiency in React and at least one automation testing framework, earned an ISTQB Foundation certificate, and grown into a mid-level engineer managing junior testers or owning a frontend module independently — with a salary trajectory that reflects every skill you committed to building.

phases.goal: Become immediately hireable for Entry-Level Manual QA roles while laying the technical foundation for automation and React — then land your first full-time offer.
actions: Create a public GitHub profile this week and push your two existing HTML/CSS/JS projects with clean READMEs, live demo links via GitHub Pages or Vercel, and a project description that explains what you built, what technologies you used, and what problem it solves — this directly addresses the thin portfolio gap flagged in your assessment.

Complete the ISTQB Foundation Level (CTFL) self-study program using the official ISTQB syllabus and free practice exams on Guru99 and Software Testing Help — schedule your exam for month 4 so it is on your CV before you apply to AvePoint, SmartOSC, and DX Tech roles that explicitly list structured QA knowledge as a requirement.

Begin a structured JavaScript fundamentals course on freeCodeCamp or The Odin Project focusing on DOM manipulation, ES6+ syntax, fetch/async-await, and array methods — complete at least 3 hours per day, 5 days per week, because React is impossible to learn well without solid vanilla JS and every frontend listing in your target set requires it.

Apply to the 5 most accessible manual QA listings in your selected set — SmartOSC Fresh Manual Tester, DX Tech Fresher/Junior Tester, VNext Fresher/Junior Tester Da Nang, TSB VN Fresher SQA, and Astraler Manual Tester — customizing each cover letter to reference your internship test cases, bug reports, and any tools you used such as JIRA, TestRail, or Postman.

Build one new portfolio project specifically designed to demonstrate QA thinking: a simple React todo or weather app (even a basic one) paired with a written test plan document covering test cases, boundary conditions, and bug report templates — host both the app and the test plan PDF on GitHub to show employers you think like a tester and can write front-end code.

Reach out to 3 professionals in Da Nang QA or frontend roles on LinkedIn each week with a specific, short message asking about their team's tech stack and hiring process — this builds a local network that directly surfaces unadvertised entry-level openings at companies like Kiaisoft and Mediastep Software.
skills: JavaScript ES6+ fundamentals (DOM, async, array methods)
Structured manual test case design and bug reporting
Git and GitHub version control for portfolio management
ISTQB Foundation Level testing theory and terminology
phases.milestone: You have received and accepted a full-time offer for an entry-level Manual QA or Junior Tester role in Da Nang, your GitHub profile has at least 3 public repositories with live demo links and professional READMEs, and your ISTQB CTFL exam is either passed or booked with a confirmed date.

phases.goal: Grow from an employed manual tester into a T-shaped engineer with demonstrable React skills and automation testing ability — making you competitive for Junior Frontend Developer and QA Engineer roles simultaneously.
actions: Enroll in a structured React course (Scrimba's React path or Bob Ziroll's free React course, then supplement with official React docs) and build a complete CRUD application with component state, useEffect, React Router, and at least one third-party API integration — deploy it live and add it to your portfolio so it directly targets listings from iViettech, Classmethod Da Nang, and FPT IS which all require ReactJS experience.

Learn Playwright or Cypress for end-to-end test automation by following the official documentation and building an automated test suite for your own React portfolio project — write at least 15 meaningful test cases covering happy paths, edge cases, and error states, then commit the test suite to GitHub so it is reviewable by employers like AvePoint and Getz who require automation skills.

Request to shadow or assist with automation tasks in your current QA role — even if your company uses manual testing only, volunteer to prototype a Playwright or Cypress script for a regression scenario and present it to your team lead as a time-saving initiative, which builds both your skill and your internal reputation as someone who drives improvement.

Build a second React project that is meaningfully different from the first — a personal finance tracker, a job application tracker, or a booking UI — using a component library like Shadcn/UI or Material UI, and integrating local storage or a simple Supabase or Firebase backend so you can speak credibly to junior fullstack conversations at companies like TECHVIFY Software.

Begin studying for and obtain one automation-relevant certificate — the Playwright or Cypress official documentation completion is not certifiable, but the ISTQB Advanced Test Automation Engineer (if budget allows) or a Udemy certificate from a highly-rated Cypress/Playwright course provides a credible, employer-visible signal of commitment.

Apply to Junior Frontend Developer and QA Engineer roles that require React or automation at the 12-month mark — target SmartOSC, FPT IS, Classmethod Da Nang, and Getz, using your two completed React projects and automated test suite as portfolio evidence, and explicitly reference the bridge between your QA background and frontend skills as your unique value.
skills: React (components, hooks, state management, React Router)
End-to-end test automation with Playwright or Cypress
REST API integration and basic backend familiarity (Supabase or Firebase)
Component library usage (Shadcn/UI or Material UI)
Git branching strategy and pull request workflow for team collaboration
phases.milestone: You have three live, public React projects in your portfolio, a committed automation test suite on GitHub with 15+ test cases, and you have applied to at least 10 Junior Frontend or QA Engineer roles — receiving at least 3 interview invitations that confirm your profile is now competitive above the entry-level floor.

phases.goal: Advance to a mid-level or senior QA Engineer or Frontend Developer role, establish technical authority in your team, and begin mentoring junior engineers — positioning yourself for a lead or architect track.
actions: Target a mid-level promotion or a lateral move to a product-focused company where you own a frontend module or a QA function end-to-end — companies like AvePoint, SmartOSC, or Orient Software offer mid-level tracks that reward engineers who can write code AND enforce quality, and your dual-track background becomes a genuine competitive advantage at this level.

Learn TypeScript deeply and integrate it into all new React projects and automation scripts — TypeScript is now the default expectation at mid-to-senior frontend and QA engineer levels across Vietnam's enterprise software companies, and this single skill upgrade will unlock a significant salary increase and access to higher-tier job listings.

Contribute to at least one open-source project related to your primary stack — a React component library, a Playwright plugin, or a testing utility — so that your GitHub profile shows collaborative, production-quality code rather than solo personal projects, which is a differentiator that senior hiring managers at companies like AvePoint and Scopic explicitly look for.

Mentor at least one junior tester or frontend intern formally — document your mentorship approach, share a learning plan you built for them, and request a LinkedIn recommendation from your mentee and your team lead — because leadership evidence is what separates mid-level candidates from senior-level offers in Vietnam's tech market.

Build and publish a technical blog or YouTube series in Vietnamese and English covering one specific topic you have mastered (e.g., 'How to write Playwright tests for React apps' or 'QA thinking for frontend developers') — two to three posts or videos positions you as a visible expert in Da Nang's tech community and generates inbound recruiter interest without you applying.

Set a concrete salary and title target for year 5 — Senior QA Engineer at 30–40M VND/month or Mid-level Frontend Developer at 25–35M VND/month — and reverse-engineer the skill gaps between your year-2 self and that target by reviewing 10 senior-level job descriptions annually, treating each gap as a training sprint to complete before the next performance review cycle.
skills: TypeScript for React and test automation codebases
System-level QA strategy (test planning, risk-based testing, CI/CD pipeline integration)
Technical mentorship and code review leadership
Advanced React patterns (custom hooks, context, performance optimization)
Professional communication and stakeholder reporting in English
phases.milestone: You hold a mid-level or senior title (QA Engineer, Frontend Developer, or equivalent) at a recognized Da Nang tech company, earn a salary of at least 25M VND per month, have formally mentored at least one junior engineer, and have a public technical presence — blog, GitHub contributions, or speaking at a local tech meetup — that demonstrates expertise beyond your job title.
